Anthropic released its latest AI model, Claude Opus 5.5. The new version comes roughly two months after the previous Opus model upgrade, in line with Anthropic's typical release cadence.

Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5

Anthropic's Claude lineup currently offers multiple AI models.

The three flagship models are Haiku (the smallest and least expensive), Sonnet (mid-sized and mid-priced), and Opus (the largest and most expensive of the three).

Beyond these are Fable/Mythos, which offer more powerful capabilities and command higher pricing, representing Anthropic's premium positioning.

This release upgrades the Opus model in the Claude family from version 5.0 to 5.5.

Anthropic stated: "Opus 5.5 is our first model released since we called for a slowdown in frontier development. As with past models, it was tested by external evaluation organisations before release, including METR and Frontier Design. It scored the highest result we have seen to date on our most comprehensive alignment assessment."

Below is Anthropic's introduction of Opus 5.5's performance:

Regarding coding, Anthropic had this to say:

Opus 5.5 is particularly adept at handling large, sprawling tasks, such as migrating and reviewing entire codebases. Earlier testers used it to review and patch a 200,000-line codebase in three hours, while Opus 5 took over 20 hours and used 2.5 times more resources. In one internal test, we had Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 translate HAProxy (software widely used to balance network traffic loads across servers) from C to Rust. Both rewrites passed nearly all of HAProxy's regression tests, but Opus 5.5 completed the task in just 9.5 hours—faster than Fable 5.1's 12 hours—and at 51% lower cost. Opus 5.5 delivers frontier-grade agentic coding performance at a fraction of the cost of its peers. On the default FrontierCode workload, it outperforms GPT-6 Astra at roughly one-fifth the cost per task. On Terminal Bench 4.0, it matches Astra at around 40% of the cost; on CursorBench, it leads GPT-5.6 Sol by 11 points at about one-third the cost.

In addition, Opus 5.5's pricing has been adjusted compared to Opus 5:

Opus 5.5 requires less computing power to run than Opus 5, and pricing reflects this accordingly. Our testing shows that, under default settings, typical workloads cost 40% less than Opus 5. Input and output tokens are priced at US$4 and US$20 per million respectively, 20% lower than Opus 5. Cache reads (which account for the majority of cost in agentic and coding workloads) are priced at US$0.20 per million tokens, 60% lower than Opus 5. Opus 5.5 also outputs more than 30% faster than Opus 5. Alongside the price reductions, we have raised the five-hour usage caps for Pro, Max, and Team plans. We are also offering usage credit resets for subscribers, who can now bank credits for use whenever they need them.

The new Claude Opus 5.5 model is now officially available. Looking ahead, Anthropic said that Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 will "be released in the coming weeks, bringing similar improvements in capability, efficiency, and safety."
